key_insight: Reinforcement learning adds little value for single-GPU batching, but it can strongly outperform hand-tuned heuristics when routing heterogeneous requests across multiple GPUs.
engineering_relevance: For production inference systems, learned policies are most justified in multi-resource scheduling problems where they can reduce head-of-line blocking and improve throughput-latency tradeoffs.
method: Model batching/routing as an MDP over queue state, request type, and GPU availability
Train REINFORCE and PPO agents in a discrete-event simulator validated with queuing theory and production traces
Compare against static batching and routing heuristics under synthetic and real bursty workloads
evidence_signal: Across Poisson, bursty, and real-world traces, the learned routing policy achieved up to 3.5x better performance than round-robin and 48% better than the strongest heuristic, while single-GPU gains were only marginal.
watch_item: Results may not translate directly if the simulator, workload mix, or SLA constraints differ from deployment, so careful validation is needed before production rollout.
paper_title: Adaptive Inference Batching using Policy Gradients
